text:
B: Hiya! Can you hear me?
A: Yes. Hello. I'm Joanne.
B: I'm Blerta. I'm in Newcastle. Where are you?
A: Frome. Somerset.
B: Oh, I've heard of Frome, someone on my course said it's dead arty?
A: It is, a bit. Lots of markets. Lots of people with opinions about bread.
B: Ha! What do you do?
A: I'm a senior carer. Shift lead in a dementia home.
B: No way. I was a care assistant for six years. Residential, older people, before I went to uni.
A: Oh. Right. So you know.
B: I know, yeah. The twelve-hour days and your feet at the end of it. Is yours all dementia?
A: Forty beds, all dementia. Erm, I do the meds rounds, care plans, run the floor. What are you studying?
B: Speech and language therapy. Second year. It was the care home that made me want to do it, honestly. There was this lady, she'd had a stroke, and she knew exactly what she wanted to say, you could see it, and it just wouldn't come out. And we'd all sort of guess, and get it wrong, and she'd get so upset. And I thought, there must be someone who knows how to help with this properly.
A: Mm. That's the worst bit, isn't it. When they're still in there and you can't reach them.
B: Yeah. Exactly that.
A: We had a speech therapist in for one of ours last year. She did more in two visits than we'd managed in a month. So. It's a good thing to do.
B: Thank you. I started late, though, I'm twenty-seven. I left sixth form to work.
A: That's not late. Honestly. I wish I'd done something like that. I sort of let it slip.
B: You could still, though?
A: Erm. Maybe. I'm doing a Level 4 at the moment, through work. We'll see. Did you find the care work helped, on the course?
B: Loads. The lecturers talk about communicating with people with dementia, and I'm sat there thinking, I've done that at three in the morning with someone who thinks I'm their sister.
A: Ha. Yes. You learn to just be the sister.
B: You do! You just go with it. What do you do to switch off? 'Cause you need something.
A: Pottery. A class on Tuesdays. And I read a lot. Library books, mostly. Thomas Hardy, I always go back to him.
B: Oh, I love the library. I read a lot of translated stuff. Japanese, Korean. And Kadare, he's Albanian, my family's from Kosovo. Partly I read him 'cause I feel I should, sorry, that sounds bad.
A: No, that's honest. That's how I feel about some of Hardy, if I'm truthful. Jude's hard work.
B: Which one should I start with, then? I've never read any.
A: Erm. Far from the Madding Crowd. It's the kindest one. And there's sheep.
B: Sheep, okay. Sold. I'll get it out this week. My overdue pile's already massive, though.
A: Mine too. I've got one on the fridge now that's—
